medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
UWSOM is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse learning environment for all students and training culturally competent physicians to care for the region's increasingly diverse population. We have programs designed to train medical students to support urban, rural, and global underserved populations, and many students engage in student-led service learning and community outreach to address health disparities. 
Our Equity & Medical Student Engagement team is committed to supporting students to become health-equity minded physicians.
The Office of Health Care Equity (OHCE) supports student programming that promote diversity and excellence in medical education, e.g., Pathways Programs, the Center for Restorative Practices, and Anti-bias/anti-racism training.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request or may be placed on a leave of absence for personal, academic, or health related issues or as a short-term intervention to allow time to manage an issue of concern. The personal and health leave policy includes pregnancy, child birth, and recovery time; time to stay at home to care for one's child; time related to recovery from illness or therapy related to illness; or time to care for a family member who needs extraordinary care. Students who take a leave of absence retain their original matriculation date. Grades and evaluations submitted prior to the leave are retained as part of the student's permanent record.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The School of Medicine seeks to provide students with the opportunities, resources and support necessary to explore and expand their personal and professional interests, build relationships and work with others, develop skills, grow as individuals, and have fun. Students at all sites can participate in student organizations that include affinity groups, specialty interests, service or policy driven missions, and chapters of national student associations. 
The School values student voices. Students are a part of our curriculum committees, they plan and lead service learning projects, and their feedback and input is sought and heard as a matter of course. 
From our curriculum to student life, you will find opportunities to build communities that engage in dynamic educational experiences that prepare you to become innovative and health-equity minded physicians of tomorrow.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The University of Washington School of medicine is fortunate to be a five-state, six-campus medical education program. At the six Foundations campuses, Anchorage, Bozeman, Laramie, Moscow, Seattle, and Spokane, students have access to people who can help and support them and connect them to the support system that is right for them. 
The School prides itself on the depth and breadth of excellent clinical educational opportunities available throughout all of the five states that comprise our WWAMI medical education program. The regional nature of our medical school allows our students to experience the entire gamut of medical care, both rural and urban, including private practice, community health care centers, community hospitals, and tertiary care hospitals, as well as opportunities to care for diverse patient populations. And, of course, cultural and recreational opportunities abound throughout the region!
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
On-campus housing is available at most Foundations sites, but the majority of students live off-campus. Average rent will vary depending on the site. 
Since we value so highly the opportunity to travel throughout the WWAMI region for clinical training, and because we see the benefits for our students' education, housing and transportation is paid for by the School during required clinical rotations.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The UWSOM has a support system in place for LGBTQ+ students. Queer Medical Student Groups such as QMed and QTSOC (Queer and Trans Students of Color) strive to ensure a welcoming, respectful and safe academic environment for LGBTQ+ students. In addition to social events organized by students, the Office of Health Care Equity (OHCE) brings in speakers and supports community building activities such as National Coming Out Day celebrations, Transgender Day of Visibility, film screenings, and faculty-student dinners. The LGBTQ Pathway also provides a number of educational opportunities, electives and experiences open to all medical students that will better prepare them to provide culturally informed care for the LGBTQ+ population.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Disability Resources and Services (DRS) office partners with students with disabilities to ensure access and inclusion across campus. It coordinates and implements accommodation programs, serving as a resource to students, faculty, and staff to support effective service delivery. DRS also provides educational outreach to promote awareness and inclusion, and offers resource and referral information to the campus community and prospective students and their families. Working individually with students, DRS establishes academic accommodations and auxiliary aids to remove environmental barriers to equitable access for all facilities, programs, and activities. More information available at: https://depts.washington.edu/uwdrs/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The health and well-being of our medical students is a top priority. To help students thrive during medical school, we offer a wide array of wellness offerings that aim to increase students’ emotional, physical and social well-being. Learning specialists and Counseling and Wellness Services are available at all regional sites for medical students. Career advisors are also on hand to guide students in specialty exploration and preparation for the residency application process. And of course, your College Faculty member can support you throughout your journey and can help you identify what kind of support you might need. More information about programs and resources can be found at: https://education.uwmedicine.org/student-affairs/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our students, faculty, and staff share a commitment to the health of the public and form a collaborative environment that is focused on the healthcare needs of our five-state WWAMI region, particularly focusing on the needs of underserved populations. Our services, resources, and programs offer holistic support to students as they grow as individuals and as future physicians.
In your College, you will be part of a growth-oriented learning environment committed to mutual support. The aim of the Colleges is to build community, one that allows for difference while learning about each other. Students collaborate and support one another through the pass/fail preclinical curriculum and beyond.
The School values diversity and inclusion and is committed to building and sustaining an academic community in which teachers, researchers, and learners achieve the knowledge, skills, and attitudes that value and embrace inclusiveness, equity, and awareness to unleash creativity and innovation.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Depending on the location of the Foundations site, students will use a variety of transportation options including public transit, carpools, or personal vehicles. All students are responsible for securing a vehicle for transportation for their clerkships.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to present a professional appearance consistent with what is expected of a physician. Closed-toe shoes must be worn in all patient care areas.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Learning specialists and free tutoring are available. Full time counselors are on staff to promote wellness and work/life balance for students and their immediate families.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students will see patients starting the first week of matriculation.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: In the Foundations Phase, there is 4 hours of instruction, four days per week. On the fifth day, students learn clinical skills and/or see actual patients in a primary care physician’s office.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations begin after the first 18 months foundations phase. Students are expected to complete part of their training outside of their foundations site.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Students in the PreMat program will review basic science concepts integral to the Foundations curriculum while learning novel study strategies to promote success in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Sessions where patients are present, laboratory sessions, and small group learning activities designated as required are mandatory. Large group lectures are not required, but attendance is expected.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The four-year curriculum is divided into three phases: foundations, patient care, and explore and focus. Specific themes (equity and inclusion, diversity, ethics, determinants of health, global population, and public health, climate health, health systems science) are woven throughout. Each student is matched to a College faculty member who serves as a mentor throughout their time in medical school. Students complete a clinical immersion program that focuses on clinical skills practice following their first Foundations course. The foundations phase utilizes a flipped classroom approach and students spend considerable time learning in small group sessions. During the summer between year one and year two, students participate in a research project with opportunities in laboratory-based research, clinical research, literature review, community-based medicine, and global health. Students have a 12-week block dedicated to preparing for the USMLE Step 1 and preparing for clerkships. The patient care phase is comprised of the required clerkships. During the explore and focus phase, students explore career options and/or to focus on special areas of interest.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
UWSOM is nationally recognized for training future primary care doctors. Programs that provide training in rural medicine and primary care include: 
Pathways ( https://www.uwmedicine.org/education/md-program/current-students/curriculum/programs/pathways ): opportunities to gain additional knowledge and certification working with vulnerable populations: Black Health Justice, Global Health, Hispanic Health, Indian Health, LGBTQ Health, and Underserved. 
TRUST ( https://education.uwmedicine.org/somrural/programs/trust/ ) is an integrated program for selected students planning careers in rural medicine. 
WRITE ( https://education.uwmedicine.org/somrural/programs/write/ ): a 18-22-week rural clinical medical training experience. 
RUOP ( https://education.uwmedicine.org/somrural/programs/ruop/ ): a 4-week, elective, immersion experience in community medicine for students in the foundations phase.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Since 1974 UW School of Medicine has ranked consistently among the top 3 schools in receipt of National Institutes of Health (NIH) grant funding. There are numerous opportunities for students to participate in research. Students involved in the Medical Scientist Research Training Program (MSRTP) could be eligible for housing and travel support.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The UW School of Medicine is a four-year program which includes 3 phases, Foundations Phase (18 months including summer), Patient Care (12 months) and Explore and Focus (15 months).
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service Learning Resource Center facilitates service learning, volunteer activities and advocacy for MD students: https://education.uwmedicine.org/student-affairs/service-learning/
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: More information about the Independent Investigative Inquiry can be found at: https://sites.uw.edu/somcurr2
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: As a regional medical school, the UWSOM has over 275 affiliated hospitals and clinics across the five state region.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: Instruction is in English. Spanish for the Health Professional is a non-clinical selective course that introduces students to intermediate medical Spanish vocabulary and medical Spanish scripts.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The UWSOM is dedicated to improving the health of the public by advancing medical knowledge, providing outstanding primary and specialty care to people of the region, and preparing tomorrow's physicians and scientists. Our nationally renown programs in family medicine and rural health are enhanced by clinical faculty who provide community-based medical education in the states of Washington, Wyoming, Alaska, Montana, and Idaho. The UWSOM is committed to building and sustaining a multi-faceted academic community and to assuring that access to education and training is open to all segments of society.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The UWSOM is dedicated to improving the general health and well-being of the public. As the pre-eminent academic medical center in our region and as a national leader in biomedical research, we place special emphasis on educating and training physicians, scientists, and allied health professionals dedicated to two distinct missions:
- Meeting the health care needs of our region, especially by recognizing the importance of primary care and providing service to underserved populations; 
- Advancing knowledge and assuming leadership in the biomedical sciences and in academic medicine.
The School has a special responsibility to the people in the states of WA, WY, AK, MT, and ID. We are committed to building and sustaining a multi-faceted academic community and to assuring that access to education and training is open to learners from all segments of society. http://www.uwmedicine.org/education/about/mission

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks before April 30th, one week thereafter
medSchoolApplication.matricNote: Note: UWSOM is a regional medical school and participates in the WWAMI program. Over 95% of matriculated students are from WA, WY, AK, MT, and ID and are considered "In-State".
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
It is strongly encouraged that letters be printed on university, company, or personal letterhead and signed. Letters of recommendation that are missing letterhead and/or signature will be given less consideration.

All letters of recommendation should be submitted via the AMCAS Letters of Evaluation/Recommendation service.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants can submit a premedical committee evaluation and up to 3 additional letters OR submit a minimum of 3 and up to 6 letters from writers who can speak to one or more of the following: academic ability, commitment to service, leadership potential, clinical or research experiences, interpersonal skills, interaction with patients, ability to function on a team, and/or potential as a physician, respect for others, compassion, maturity, communication skill, work ethic.

The collection of letters should provide a balanced and well-rounded view of your candidacy for medicine.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants will have an opportunity to learn more about the University of Washington School of Medicine during their interview week. Activities include meeting students, faculty, and administrators who are part of the diverse UWSOM community.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations will go out in the beginning of September. Applicants at regional sites can expect an invitation at least three weeks before the interview week for their state.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat:
A three-member panel interviews each applicant.

More information available at: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/admissions/interview
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be virtual (video) interviews.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: WWAMI DACA students are considered for the MD only program if they are verified as state residents in their state and eligible for WWAMI funding. All others must have U.S. citizenship or green card.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: The requirements to establish state residency will vary throughout the WWAMI region. It is difficult to become a state resident after matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Non-WWAMI applicants must have WWAMI ties and meet mission-based criteria. Wyoming, Alaska, Montana, and Idaho residents are considered in-state. Visit uwmedicine.org/admissions for details.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: WWAMI DACA students are considered for the MD only program if they are verified in their state as eligible for WWAMI funding. Students should check with their respective state certifying officers.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The University of Washington School of Medicine (UWSOM) does not accept applications from students who request to transfer from other medical school. More information is available at: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/admissions/transfer-advanced-standing 

Applicants are expected to comply with the following policies:

Clerkship Policy: The UWSOM takes pride in the vast array of clinical educational opportunities available to our students throughout the WWAMI region. Our Clerkship Policy enables students to take advantage of these opportunities. Students are expected to spend 24 weeks of their required clerkships outside of a 50-mile radius from Seattle, and regional or Spokane students spend a minimum of 8 weeks within Seattle. Exceptions to this policy are granted rarely.

Essential Requirements: The M.D. degree is recognized as a broad, undifferentiated degree requiring the acquisition of general knowledge and basic skills in all fields of medicine. The education of a physician requires assimilation of knowledge, acquisition of skills and development of judgment through patient care experience in preparation for independent and appropriate decisions required in practice. There are numerous components to the UWSOM Essential Requirements of Medical Education: Admission, Retention, Promotion, and Graduation Standards. See the complete technical standards at: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/admissions/expectations 

UW Medicine Policy on Professional Conduct: UW Medicine is committed to high standards of professionalism in patient care, research and education among our faculty, staff, residents, fellows and students. Professionalism is integral to our mission of improving health, and includes demonstrating excellence, respect, integrity, compassion, altruism and accountability in all endeavors and creating an environment supportive of diversity in ideas, perspectives and experiences. Read the UW Medicine Policy on Professional Conduct at: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/admissions/expectations 

Health Sciences Immunization Program (HSIP) Policy: Students agree to meet immunization and TB screening requirements in accordance with CDC guidelines for healthcare personnel and as outlined by the Health Sciences Immunization Program (HSIP). This includes a requirement that students be vaccinated against COVID-19: https://www.ehs.washington.edu/system/files/resources/HSIP-imm-req-policy.pdf 

Applicants are expected to communicate directly with the Admissions Office and the AAMC Choose Your Medical School Tool regarding their decision. On April 15, applicants must narrow medical school selections down to three. On April 30, applicants MUST select either “Commit to Enroll”, “Plan to Enroll”, or withdraw their application at the University of Washington. On June 14, applicants accepted to the program MUST select "Commit to Enroll" at the University of Washington in the AMCAS Application and withdraw their application from all other programs. If a decision is not reported by this date, it will be interpreted as a withdrawal. The UWSOM will not accept/enroll any applicant who chooses to "Commit to Enroll" at another institution. Alternates that have "Commit to Enroll" at another institution will not be accepted. Offers of admission will still be made to applicants that "Plan to Enroll" at another program.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The most recent MCAT score will be used for the initial automated academic screening. After the academic screen, all lifetime scores will be visible to the admissions committee. As part of the holistic admissions process, the score will be considered in context with grades and the rest of the application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
The UWSOM uses an automated MCAT screen. 

Minimum MCAT cutoff varies every year. 
E-26 Cutoff for WWAMI: minimum latest total score of 498
E-26 Cutoff for Non-WWAMI: minimum latest total score of 500
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo:
The UWSOM uses an automated GPA screen.

Minimum GPA cutoff varies every year. 
E-26 Cutoff for WWAMI: minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0
E-26 Cutoff for non-WWAMI: minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.25 

All applicants must have a minimum science GPA of 3.0
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo:
Minimum GPA cutoff varies every year. 
E-26 Cutoff for WWAMI: minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0
E-26 Cutoff for non-WWAMI: minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.25 

All applicants must have a minimum science GPA of 3.0

If an applicant demonstrates an upward trajectory in their graduate or postbacc coursework and they believe they were rejected due to their undergraduate grades, they can request a manual screen of their application
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All postbacc or graduate coursework will be considered by the Admissions Committee during the screening for a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college coursework is accepted for fulfilling premedical course requirements.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: UWSOM tries to make our process as equitible as possible. We want all applicants to be considered based on the application and the interview, so to be sure no applicant has different materials than another, we do not letters of intent, activities updates, or thank you notes. Grades updates are permitted via official transcripts.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
The University of Washington School of Medicine (UWSOM) maintains a strong institutional commitment to training medical students to provide excellent care to a diverse patient population. The UWSOM provides equal educational opportunities for qualified students with disabilities who apply for admission to the MD program or who are already enrolled. The technical standards are not intended to deter any candidate for whom reasonable accommodation will allow fulfillment of the complete curriculum.

As an accredited medical school, the University of Washington School of Medicine adheres to the accreditation standards described by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education in “Functions and Structure of a Medical School.”

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Financial status has no bearing on admission. Most aid is in the form of loans. All applicants must submit a FAFSA to apply for financial aid. The online application is available in January (  https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa  ). 

The deadline is January 15 regardless of admission status. After the deadline, students can still be considered for Stafford loans and Grad Plus loans. More information is available at http://www.uwmedicine.org/financialaid

medSchoolPrograms.info:
SHPEP at the UW is committed to improving access to quality healthcare. The University of Washington program involves rigorous academic enrichment through classes that provide a strong knowledge base in the basic foundational sciences and statistics. It is best suited for students completing their first year of college who are about to take these courses or those who have taken them already and feel that they could use some additional help mastering these subjects.

The SHPEP curriculum at the University of Washington is designed to build on the students’ knowledge of the social determinants of health and health disparities through the lens of social justice.

For more information, please visit: https://equity.uwmedicine.org/shpep/

All departments and interdisciplinary programs at UW are open to MSTP students for their PhD research, and our students take full advantage of the diversity of disciplines represented here. Any MSTP student and mentor may choose to work together. Details of the departments in which our students presently or recently completed their PhD studies are listed with links to their websites: https://mstp.washington.edu/program/departments/

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: If choosing our medical school as the only acceptance you are holding, select "Commit to Enroll" or "Plan to Enroll" in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tools by this date. If you remain on an alternate list at another school, you must select "Plan to Enroll."
Accepted applicants must complete all prerequisite courses.
Accepted applicants must submit all required official transcripts to the Office of Admissions.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: The number of waitlist positions vary each year by the regional state and are determined by the competitiveness of the applicant pool.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Alternates are accepted off an alternate list as positions become available in the entering class. Wyoming, Alaska, Montana, Idaho, Spokane, and Seattle cohorts have separate alternate lists.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Please visit our website for the most up to date prerequisite information: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/admissions/course-requirements
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no time limit on coursework that can be used towards fulfilling the prerequisites.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Candidates are considered comparatively on academic performance, motivation, maturity, integrity, understanding social determinants of health, and leadership. Demonstrated community service, communication skills, knowledge of issues in health care delivery, ability to think analytically, and intellectual curiosity are also important. Preference is given to residents of WWAMI; less than 5% of the class is from outside the WWAMI region. Competitive candidates are asked to send additional materials. Criminal background check is required. Only U.S. citizens or permanent residents are considered. WWAMI DACA students are considered for the MD program if they are verified as state residents in their state. Applicants with an interest in research may apply for the MD/PhD program regardless of state of legal residency and must have U.S. citizenship or permanent residency. Candidates may apply up to 3 times. All eligible applicants are encouraged to apply.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
Clinical experiences are an important way for applicants to gain a richer understanding of medicine and can help ground an applicant’s decision to apply to medical school before investing considerable time and money. When considering clinical experiences, our admissions committee is looking to understand what applicants have learned about medicine and about themselves. The quality of the reflection on your experiences in your application tells the committee far more about your understanding of medicine than the quantity of hours you have accumulated.

For more guidance, go to: https://www.uwmedicine.org/school-of-medicine/resources/clinical-experiences
